findings.reason: the section must name which owner defines "landed" and reconcile the other two, or a plan whose sections are declared done without a collapse is gated on the wrong content.
findings.text: §16's coverage predicate needs a "not yet landed" determination and names only `landed_section_ids` (the visual collapse), but `reckon/crew/promotion.py:7212` `_landed_sections` (a section carrying a `c-run-` landing comment) and the `section_declarations` `done` status map (`reckon/_store.py:2799`) are two further definitions of the same question, and they already disagree in this very plan (its §5–§8 are declared `done` with no landed card, so `landed_section_ids` reports them unlanded) — a coverage predicate keyed on the wrong notion silently drops authored sections from the question the gate asks

findings.reason: the section should specify the mode parameter, its default and the third form's computation, and count the signature change in its interface accounting rather than stating that nothing beyond one definition is added.
findings.text: §16 says the identity digest and the prose walk "keep their names and gain a mode" and that "nothing is retired", but `plan_fingerprint(plan, *, legacy: bool = False)` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:368`) currently carries a two-valued flag and the change needs three recognisable forms — the section-set digest (new current), the pre-collapse digest (existing `legacy=True`) and the present whole-document digest (new third form added to `_fingerprint_forms`, `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:598`) — so a boolean cannot express it, the public signature must change (mode value plus new default), and every `plan_fingerprint(..., legacy=)` caller is affected; the interface accounting counts only the coverage predicate

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the consolidation moves section identity behind one raw-text enumerator (`_StructuredSectionSpanParser`) whose interface (identity, heading text, replaced span as offsets) hides the wrapper-vs-heading id resolution, the structured-region exclusion and the offset computation, and it deletes the hand-rolled depth counters in `_AuthoredProseParser` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:188-234`); that is a smaller interface over more hidden behaviour than the current three walkers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16's coverage predicate re-derives a "has this section landed" test while three owners of that question already exist, and §16 names only one of them.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1475, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 states it adds one public definition and retires nothing, but the change also adds a third value to the public `plan_fingerprint` mode space, which the section's interface accounting does not count or name.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §16 names and extends existing owners (`_StructuredSectionSpanParser` in `reckon/_plan_html.py`, `_authored_section_headings` in `reckon/mcp_views.py`, `_section_heading`/`_section_body_end`/`landed_section_ids` in `reckon/_store.py`, `plan_fingerprint`/`_authored_prose`/`_fingerprint_forms` in `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`) rather than proposing a fresh scanner, and all five cited mechanisms exist as described.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the coverage predicate is a genuinely different query from `read_plan_review`'s single-record join (it asks whether *every* unlanded section is covered by *some* stored review, not which review matches one digest), so introducing it beside the reader is not a wrapper over the reader, and the plan states the reuse (`_fingerprint_forms`) it extends.
